definitions.explanation: Used with negative expressions to mean "not at all" or "absolutely not." Emphasizes complete absence or denial.
Refers to everything without exception. Often used with nouns to mean "all of something."

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}のことは{一切|いっさい}{知|し}らない。
examples.english: I don't know anything about him at all.

examples.japanese: {責任|せきにん}は{一切|いっさい}{負|お}いません。
{費用|ひよう}は{一切|いっさい}{会社|かいしゃ}が{負担|ふたん}します。
examples.english: The company will cover all expenses.

notes:
TWO MAIN USES:

1) WITH NEGATIVE: Emphasizes complete absence
・{一切|いっさい}〜ない (not 〜 at all)
・{一切|いっさい}{関係|かんけい}ない (have nothing to do with)
・{一切|いっさい}{責任|せきにん}を{負|お}わない (take no responsibility whatsoever)

2) AS NOUN: Everything, all
・{一切|いっさい}の{費用|ひよう} (all expenses)
・{一切|いっさい}を{任|まか}せる (to entrust everything)
・{一切|いっさい}{合切|がっさい} (everything without exception - emphatic)

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
・{一切|いっさい}お{断|ことわ}りします (We refuse absolutely)
・{一切|いっさい}ノーコメント (No comment at all)

LEGAL/BUSINESS USAGE:
{一切|いっさい} is commonly used in disclaimers, contracts, and formal notices to express absolute terms.

ORIGIN:
From Buddhist terminology meaning "all things" or "everything."
